small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_HW (512) and try num_warps=16; the inner loop has 27 tl.dot calls of shape (OC=64, IC=16) x (IC=16, BLOCK_HW), which is compute-heavy and benefits from wider tiles to amortize weight loads.
- Hoist the weight loads: load all 27 (kd,kh,kw) weight tiles once outside the d_out loop (they don't depend on d_out), and reuse across the D=32 outer iterations to cut weight memory traffic ~32x.
- Swap the loop order to (kd, kh, kw, d_out) so for each kernel tap the same weight tile feeds D accumulators; keep separate acc[d_out] only if needed, or alternatively keep current order but cache the 9 (kh,kw) weight tiles per kd in registers.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an im2col-style GEMM: one program tile per (B, OC_tile, HW_tile), with the K dimension being IC*kh*kw=144 and the D axis accumulated inside (since mean collapses it). Issue tl.dot on (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K) x (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_HW) with proper tiling instead of the current (OC=64 full) x (BLOCK_HW) shape — this lets BLOCK_HW grow and uses tensor cores more efficiently.
- Move to channels_last (NHWC-like) input layout for the H,W spatial gathers so IC-vector loads are contiguous; precompute h_in/w_in offset tables outside the d_out loop.
- Consider splitting the kernel into two stages when occupancy is the bottleneck: stage 1 produces (B, OC, H, W) summed-over-D conv output via a tiled GEMM; stage 2 fuses bias+softmax+tanh+scale across channels. The current single-kernel design forces OC=64 to be a full tile dimension which limits BLOCK_HW; a two-stage design decouples these.
